bulk_helper.role: shared fixed-record charge helper: performs the mode-1 charge of 0x800 and, when the charge and the remaining width allow, copies 0x800 bytes from the cursor into its result at +0x1. Its result byte at +0x0 is 0 on success and 1 on failure, with +0x8 holding 2 for a charge refusal and 0 for a shortfall (the additional count then at +0x10). Recorded as a called boundary of bulk_b, not a traced owner.

boundaries.field1_5_readers: copies 0x2cd7bb0/0x5821340 and the slow reader 0x5822710 are the owners of the open field1-5 reader packet (#2422); recorded here only as call targets
boundaries.memcpy_slot: GOT slot 0x64df508, R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT against the dynamic symbol memcpy (glibc); bulk_a and the helper call through the slot, bulk_b loads the pointer from the slot and calls it four times
boundaries.twin_helpers: the helpers at 0x232cd90 and 0x58251a0 that receive the twin addresses are not traced; whether they forward a state unchanged is outside this packet
boundaries.u32_readers: copies 0x2cd79c0/0x5821150 are the owners of the open u32 reader packet (#2412); recorded here only as call targets
boundaries.u64_readers: copies 0x2cd7ac0/0x5821250 are owned by the open u64 reader packet (#2300); no call to either occurs in the traced functions

bulk_a.record_header_bytes: 0x17 bytes copied field by field from the cursor before the payload copy (0x17 + 0x7e9 = 0x800)

bulk_b.bulk_copies: four staged copies of 0x800 bytes: result +0x1 to rsp+0x1808 to rsp+0x1008 to rsp+0x808 to output +0x8

cross_family.finding: each twin calls the u32 reader first and the field1-5 reader later in the same invocation, both times with the identical state pointer (its entry argument) and the identical result buffer (rsp+0x18): one input stream through one state can therefore produce a field1 2 error from the first read and a field1 5 error from the second. No u64-family call occurs in any of the four owners, so the field1 2/3 results of that family are not produced on these states inside the traced functions. bulk_a is also called by a function (0x2ce1dc0) that first reads a u32 discriminant on the same state it passes on.

bulk_a.note: all three sites sit in FDE 0x2ce1dc0..0x2ce2a32 and pass that function's own entry state argument (r14); the same function first calls the u32 copy-a reader at 0x2ce1e0c on that state

bulk_b.note: all three sites sit in FDE 0x4e05c10..0x4e05dd8 and pass that function's own entry state argument (r15); the function repeats the call, copying each non-terminal result out, until a result with first dword 1 arrives

twin_a.note: the referencing function passes the twin address in rdx, with a stack result buffer in rdi, to a helper call at 0x2dd299a (target 0x232cd90); the helper is a boundary, its forwarding is not traced

twin_b.note: same shape as twin_a: helper call at 0x4de622a (target 0x58251a0), a boundary

bulk_a_inline.rule: charged + 0x800 is stored before the compare; refusal iff the NEW charged count > limit, i.e. success iff charged + 0x800 <= limit
bulk_a_inline.subject: the fixed 0x800-byte record

bulk_helper.rule: same store-before-compare rule as the bulk_a inline block: refusal iff the new charged count > limit
bulk_helper.subject: the fixed 0x800-byte record

twin_inline.committed_before_charge: the read itself: cursor +4 and remaining -4 are stored before the mode test, so a charge refusal still leaves the state advanced by four bytes; the flag byte that follows is charge-gated
twin_inline.rule: charged + 1 is stored before the compare; refusal iff the OLD charged count >= limit, i.e. success iff charged + 1 <= limit
twin_inline.subject: the inline four-byte read

inline_charges.uniform_bound: every charge traced here and in the reader packets (#2412 charge 4, #2422/#2300 charge 8) succeeds under the same bound: new charged count <= limit

limits: Static trace only: no pinned bytes were executed and no live node, network, signer, or exchange state was used. The reader state is the five-field layout of the field1-5 reader packet (mode +0x0, limit +0x8, cursor +0x10, remaining +0x18, charged count +0x20); field names are that packet record, re-validated here only where these bytes touch the fields. Who first writes the mode and limit fields is not established: every traced function forwards a state it received, and the two twins are reached only through a helper call whose forwarding is recorded as a boundary, not traced. Rawtag and result values are raw bytes; which Rust enum variants they name is not established. No Rust reconstruction is included or claimed.

reader_state.charged_count: state +0x20, u64; the mode-1 charge ledger the inline blocks and the helper add to
reader_state.cursor: state +0x10, pointer; advanced by the readers, by the twin inline read and by the bulk record reads
reader_state.limit: state +0x8, u64; read by the same charge blocks; written by none of the traced functions
reader_state.mode: state +0x0, dword; read by the twin and bulk_a inline charge blocks and by the helper (== 1 test); written by none of the traced functions
reader_state.remaining: state +0x18, u64; decremented alongside the cursor
